reader.notes: Witness g85_bf05_06 matches its golden at --std 85. The even branch forms (b+c)/2 exactly ((b+c)x5 at scale+1 in MedianScaled and MedianWide; HalfSum in ExactValue Median), so 999999999999999999 and 999999999999999998 average to ...998.5 with no overflow; parity is decided at run time, so one ALL reference over an ODO table gives the mean at counts 4 and 6 and the middle at 1 and 5.

refuter.evidence: Even branch of CobolIntrinsics.ExactValue.cs#Median: exact HalfSum of two fixed-point middles; binary64 mean only when a MIDDLE is binary64. Probes r1-002 at --std 85: EVFX MEDIAN(.1 .5 SQRT(100) 0)=.300000 (binary64 outside the middle pair does not taint the exact mean), EVMX MEDIAN(.1 SQRT(.25) 0 10)=.300000, EVRR MEDIAN(SQRT(.01) SQRT(.25))=.300000, T18E MEDIAN(SV9(18) 1e-18, 2e-18)=.000000000000000001 (1.5e-18 truncated by receiver), BGTE MEDIAN(999999999999999999 1e-18) integer part 499999999999999999 and BGTF the same minus 499999999999999999 = .500000000000000000 (37-digit exact mean, no overflow), BGT4 4 args across +-max and 1e-18/2e-18 -> mean of the 2 tiny middles, PSCE MEDIAN(SPPP9 .0001, S9P(3) 5000)=2500.000050, MZER (-0 0 1 -1) -> 0, ROUN COMPUTE ROUNDED PIC 9 = MEDIAN(1 2) -> 2 and TRUN -> 1 (the 1.5 is carried, not cut), c4 TE(ALL) TE(ALL) 10 occurrences -> 4. DIV MEDIAN(1/3 2/3)=.499999 matches plain COMPUTE (1/3+2/3)/2 = .499999 (d1-001): arithmetic-expression arguments' intermediate precision is implementor latitude per A.2.3 GR2, not a MEDIAN defect.
